subject: english-literature
topicDisplay: Paper 1 Shakespeare And The 19th Century Novel
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In A Christmas Carol, what is Scrooge's famous dismissive exclamation about Christmas?
questions.explain: Scrooge repeatedly snaps "Bah! Humbug!", showing his contempt for Christmas cheer and generosity.

questions.q: Before meeting Juliet, with whom is Romeo lovesick at the play's opening?
questions.explain: Romeo pines for Rosaline, who does not return his love, until he sees Juliet and forgets her entirely.

questions.q: What dramatic device does Shakespeare use in the Prologue when it calls Romeo and Juliet 'a pair of star-crossed lovers'?
questions.explain: The Prologue foreshadows the lovers' doomed, fated deaths from the outset.

questions.q: What plan does Friar Lawrence give Juliet to avoid marrying Paris?
options: To run away to Mantua alone
To confess the secret marriage publicly
To drink a potion that makes her appear dead
questions.explain: He gives her a sleeping potion to feign death so she can later escape with Romeo.

questions.q: How does the Elizabethan belief in fate and the stars shape the play's tone?
options: It suggests the lovers freely control their destiny
It frames the lovers as "star-crossed", doomed by forces beyond their control
It implies the feud can never end
It shows religion has no role
questions.explain: Elizabethan audiences believed the stars influenced human lives, so the "star-crossed" lovers seem fated for tragedy.

questions.q: What good comes from the lovers' deaths at the play's close?
options: The Prince seizes both family estates
Verona is freed from the plague
questions.explain: The grieving families finally end their feud, reconciled by the tragedy they caused.

questions.q: Which character secretly marries Romeo and Juliet, hoping to end the feud?
questions.explain: Friar Lawrence weds them in secret, believing their union may reconcile the two families.

questions.q: In the famous balcony scene, what does Juliet mean by "wherefore art thou Romeo?"
options: She questions whether he is real
She asks where Romeo is hiding
She laments that he is a Montague, an enemy of her family
She wonders why he loves her
questions.explain: "Wherefore" means "why"; Juliet wishes Romeo were not a Montague so their families' feud would not divide them.

questions.q: How old is Juliet in the play, reflecting Elizabethan attitudes to marriage?
questions.explain: Juliet is not yet fourteen, and her father pushes an early marriage, reflecting period customs around young brides.

questions.q: In Romeo and Juliet, which character urges calm and tries to keep the peace, refusing to fight Tybalt before Mercutio intervenes?
questions.explain: Romeo refuses to fight the newly-related Tybalt, prompting Mercutio to duel in his place.

questions.q: How does the Prologue describe Romeo and Juliet?
questions.explain: The Chorus calls them "a pair of star-crossed lovers", introducing the theme of fate.

questions.q: How does Juliet die at the end of the play?
options: She drinks the Friar's potion again
She stabs herself with Romeo's dagger
questions.explain: Waking to find Romeo dead, Juliet stabs herself with his dagger.

questions.q: Why does the Friar's crucial letter never reach Romeo in Mantua?
options: Friar John is quarantined and cannot deliver it
questions.explain: Friar John is held up by a plague quarantine, so Romeo never learns Juliet's death is faked.

questions.q: In Romeo and Juliet, at whose party do Romeo and Juliet first meet?
questions.explain: Romeo gatecrashes the Capulets' masked ball, where he meets Juliet and instantly falls in love.

questions.q: What does Romeo do immediately after Mercutio is killed?
options: He returns home to his parents
He begs the Prince for mercy
questions.explain: Enraged by Mercutio's death, Romeo kills Tybalt and is consequently banished.

questions.q: Whom does Lord Capulet intend Juliet to marry, against her wishes?
questions.explain: Capulet arranges for Juliet to marry the wealthy young Count Paris, brushing aside her secret marriage to Romeo.

questions.q: What is the role of Prince Escalus in Verona?
options: He is the ruler who tries to keep peace and punishes the feuding families
questions.explain: Prince Escalus governs Verona, threatens death for further brawling, and finally banishes Romeo for killing Tybalt.

questions.q: In the vision of the future, how do people react to the unnamed dead man's belongings?
options: They steal and sell his possessions without grief
questions.explain: Scavengers, including his charwoman, sell off the dead Scrooge's bed-curtains and clothes, showing how unloved he was.

questions.q: In Romeo and Juliet, which two feuding families does the play centre on?
questions.explain: The ancient grudge between the Montagues and Capulets frames the tragedy.

questions.q: What is the Nurse's role in Juliet's life?
options: She is Juliet's confidante and former wet-nurse
She is Lady Capulet's servant only
She is a spy for the Montagues
questions.explain: The Nurse raised Juliet and acts as her trusted confidante and go-between with Romeo.

questions.q: What does the murder of a king represent in the play's idea of kingship and the divine right of kings?
options: A crime against the natural and divine order
questions.explain: Killing Duncan, God's anointed king, violates the divine order, reflected in the unnatural disturbances that follow.

questions.q: Who kills Mercutio in the play?
questions.explain: Tybalt fatally stabs Mercutio under Romeo's arm, prompting Mercutio's curse "A plague o' both your houses!".
